drills.q: Why can't a cross-encoder search a 10M-document corpus directly?
drills.a: Its score is a function of the query-document pair jointly, so nothing can be precomputed; scoring the whole corpus per query would require 10M forward passes, infeasible at interactive latency.

drills.q: Give real numbers for Cohere rerank-3.5's cost and latency, and BGE-reranker-v2-m3's latency.
drills.a: Cohere rerank-3.5: $2/1K searches, +80-150ms p50 (real e2e ~600ms w/ network). BGE-reranker-v2-m3: GPU 50-100ms, CPU ~130ms per 16-pair batch, open weights.

drills.q: A reranker was added and offline eval improved, but production p99 blew the SLA. What happened and how do you fix it?
drills.a: Likely reranking too many candidates (k1 too large) synchronously in the request path. Fix: reduce k1 to the recall-plateau point, batch reranker calls, reconsider whether all candidates truly need reranking.

drills.q: A reranker fails to improve answer quality even though it's working correctly. How do you diagnose this?
drills.a: Measure recall@k1 of the first stage alone against a labeled eval set; if the gold chunk isn't in the candidate set, the reranker is blameless -- the fix is in retrieval, not reranking.

drills.q: Explain ColBERT-style late interaction as an alternative to full cross-encoder reranking, including its cost.
drills.a: Keeps token-level embeddings for query and doc, aggregates via MaxSim (each query token attends to its best-matching doc token); doc token embeddings are precomputable, giving much of cross-encoder precision at lower query-time compute -- but costs far more index storage (one vector per token vs one per doc).

drills.q: Design a three-stage retrieval cascade for a high-value use case like legal document search.
drills.a: Stage 1: hybrid search (BM25+bi-encoder+RRF) for high recall, ~150-300 candidates. Stage 2: cross-encoder rerank down to top 10-20. Stage 3 (gated to high-value queries only, given cost): LLM-as-judge pass over the final handful for precision.

drills.q: Design the reranking strategy for a multi-tenant SaaS product with tenant corpora from a few hundred to millions of documents, under a shared latency SLA.
drills.a: Small tenants may need no reranking stage at all (little ranking error to fix); large tenants get the standard cascade with k1 tuned per-tenant against their own recall@k1 curve. Model cost as queries/sec * k1 * cost_per_candidate per tenant rather than a flat line item.

drills.q: What silent truncation bug affects cross-encoder reranking of long documents, and how do you catch it?
drills.a: The concatenated query+document pair silently truncates at the model's max sequence length (often 512 tokens), hurting accuracy on chunks needing the most context. Catch it by monitoring truncation rate as an explicit metric, since it won't surface as an obvious error.
